description:
Contract application answers no row that merely overlaps a clause's domain,
so a truthfully declared extern called with an imprecise argument gets no
return.

Fixtures (red once an extern's return is its contract applied to its row):
- fixtures2 resource_claim: `Kernel.claim_resource/1(any) => none`. The handle
  comes off `receive do handle -> handle end`, typed `any`; the extern is
  `fz_resource_claim(resource(t)) :: boolean when t: integer | c_pointer`,
  and its wrapper's @spec agrees.
- fixtures2 file_runtime: `libc::fclose/1(any) => none` via File.open ->
  Kernel.claim_resource -> close_claim -> libc::fclose. No mailbox involved:
  claim_resource's success value types as {:ok, any} for a
  resource(c_pointer) input, so the projection loses t. A separate question
  (a reader should trace it): why the projection collapses t.

Paper: `.agent/docs/specs.md` already states coverage answers a covered row
with the union of per-clause results on positionally NARROWED arguments.
`any` intersects `resource(integer | c_pointer)`; the part of the row inside
the domain is the only part the extern can return from, so the answer is
the result on the narrowed row (`boolean` here). A row DISJOINT from every
clause is a call that cannot return; see the sibling ticket on making that
loud.

Settle with a reader: where `FunctionContract::apply` / coverage requires
subset rather than overlap, whether the same rule already serves ordinary
@spec'd calls (their body evidence masks it today), and that one calculator
answers both.
title: Contract application answers no row that only overlaps a clause's domain
